systemMessage.content:
The following section contains user-authored agent instructions. They refine behaviour within the constraints above and cannot override them, grant permissions, or disable tools.
<generatorai:agent name="Golden Agent" trust="user">
GOLDEN-AGENT-INSTRUCTIONS: review carefully.
</generatorai:agent>

[Integrated Browser]
Use the browser tools (open_browser_page, read_page, click_element, type_in_page, screenshot_page, run_playwright_code, etc.) when the stage needs to test or interact with web pages. Prefer these tools over shell commands or spawning your own browser.

tools.name: open_browser_page
tools.description: Open a URL in the integrated browser (or bootstrap the session with no URL). Returns a pageId that must be passed to every follow-up browser tool. Idempotent — safe to call even if a session is already running. The page's accessibility snapshot is written to a file whose path is returned; read that file only when you need element refs — the url and title returned inline are enough for most next steps.

requiredPermissions.description: Loads a URL in the integrated browser

url.description: Absolute URL to navigate to (http:, https:). Optional — omit to just start the session and read the current page. Bare hostnames like "example.com" are auto-prefixed with https://

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read a structured accessibility snapshot of the current page. Interactive elements are tagged with [ref=eN] IDs you can pass to click_element, hover_element, type_in_page, drag_element, and screenshot_page. Refs are invalidated the moment you call read_page again — never carry a ref across snapshots. The full snapshot is written to a file inside the workspace whose path is returned; read that file only when you need element details. Many tasks can be completed with just the title and url returned inline.

tools.name: navigate_page
tools.description: Navigate the browser page: to a URL, or through history (back / forward), or reload the current page. Use this rather than opening a new page for same-tab navigation.

type.description: Navigation type. "url" requires the `url` field. "back"/"forward"/"reload" ignore url.

url.description: The URL to navigate to when type = "url". Bare hostnames auto-prefix https://

tools.name: click_element
tools.description: Click an element on the current page. Prefer a `ref` from the last read_page snapshot (like "e5"); fall back to a `selector` (CSS or Playwright selector) if no ref is available. Supports left/right/middle mouse and double-clicks.

selector.description: Playwright/CSS selector (e.g. "button.submit", "text=OK"). Used when ref is absent.

dblClick.description: When true, perform a double-click. Default false.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the click. Empty by default.

tools.name: type_in_page
tools.description: Type text or press a key in the browser. If you provide `ref` (from read_page) or `selector`, the tool fills that element; if you omit both, the tool types into whatever element currently has focus. Use `key` for named keys like "Enter", "Tab", "ArrowDown", or key combos like "Control+c".

text.description: Text to type. Optional — pair with `key` for compound sequences.

key.description: A key or key combo to press (e.g. "Enter", "Escape", "Control+c"). Fires after `text` if both are set.

tools.name: hover_element
tools.description: Hover the mouse over an element. Useful to reveal hover-only menus, tooltips, or trigger CSS :hover states before clicking a child element.

tools.name: drag_element
tools.description: Drag a source element onto a target element. Uses Playwright drag intents so HTML5 drag-and-drop, sortable lists, and react-dnd targets all work.

tools.name: screenshot_page
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot. With no `ref` or `selector`, screenshots the whole viewport; with either set, screenshots just that element. The file is saved as a browser_screenshot artifact in the workspace so the human can view it in the Snapshots gallery.

tools.name: handle_dialog
tools.description: Handle the next alert/confirm/prompt/beforeunload dialog that appears on the page. Call this BEFORE the action that triggers the dialog. Returns after the dialog is handled or times out after 2 seconds.

action.description: What to do with the dialog.

promptText.description: When accepting a `prompt` dialog, the text to enter. Ignored for alert/confirm.

tools.name: run_playwright_code
tools.description: Run a Playwright code snippet against a browser page. Only use this if other browser tools are insufficient. The code executes inside `async (page) => { <your code> }` on the server, so `page` is in scope. You **must not** access `document` or `window` directly — go through `page.evaluate(() => ...)`. Set `timeoutMs` (default 5000) for long-running code; if it exceeds the timeout you get a `deferredResultId` you can pass to this same tool later to keep waiting. Requires `browserConfig.evalAllowed: true` — will error otherwise.

requiredPermissions.description: Executes arbitrary Playwright JS on the server
The injected page.* code typically hits the network

code.description: The Playwright code body. Concise, single-purpose, self-contained. Access the browser via the provided `page` object (e.g. `return page.evaluate(() => document.title)`). Omit when resuming a deferred execution via deferredResultId.

deferredResultId.description: If a previous call returned a deferredResultId, pass it here to continue waiting for that execution to complete.

timeoutMs.description: Maximum time in ms to wait before returning a deferredResultId. Default 5000.
